transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

My thoughts jump all over the place and I can’t keep a straight line when I talk or plan anything anymore. It has become so frustrating because I just can't seem to manage my daily routine or organize my responsibilities like I used to.
Have you also experienced any significant feelings of anxiety or worry that interfere with your daily life, or is it mainly the disorganization and jumping thoughts that are bothering you?

It is definitely the disorganization and my jumping thoughts that are the overwhelming issue, rather than typical anxiety. My mind constantly ricochets from my mother's medical appointments to old paintings or train schedules, making it impossible to hold a coherent conversation or finish a plan. I just end up feeling incredibly scattered and frustrated.
Do you also experience periods of excessive restlessness, fidgeting, or an inability to stay seated, especially when you're trying to focus or engage in quiet activities?

Yes, I struggle immensely with sitting still and feel incredibly restless. During my high-energy phases, I pace endlessly back and forth from the kitchen to the living room, completely unable to sit down long enough to finish anything. Instead of focusing, I just race around the apartment cleaning and reorganizing old files.
Can you tell me if your restlessness and hyperactivity are more prominent, or is it the difficulty with sustaining attention and following through on instructions that causes you the most trouble?

Honestly, both are severe and they feel deeply intertwined, so it's hard to say which is worse because they constantly feed into each other. My physical restlessness drives me to pace and start elaborate projects like cleaning or planning a festival, but then my extreme distractibility kicks in and I can't follow through on any of it. They just collide and leave me completely unable to finish anything.
Can you describe a situation where you were able to focus and complete a task without getting distracted, and if so, what factors helped you stay on track?

I honestly cannot think of any recent situation where I was able to stay focused and actually complete a task. My mind constantly jumps around from one thought to the next, and nothing I try seems to help me stay on track anymore. It is incredibly frustrating because it feels like I've completely lost the ability to see anything through to the end.
Can you tell me if your symptoms of inattention and hyperactivity have been present and caused significant impairment since childhood, or did they develop more recently in adulthood?

These symptoms are entirely new and only started about ten months ago, after I retired to help care for my mother. I never had any issues like this as a child or during my long career as a museum curator, where I was actually known for being very meticulous, organized, and focused.
Can you confirm that before the onset of these symptoms ten months ago, you had no history of significant inattention or hyperactivity that caused problems in your daily life or relationships?

Yes, I can absolutely confirm that. Before these past ten months, I was highly organized and known for my meticulous planning of museum exhibitions and community projects. I successfully managed a very demanding career and an active lifestyle with absolutely no history of inattention or hyperactivity.

You mentioned that these symptoms started about ten months ago, after your retirement. Can you tell me more about what you think might have triggered this change, considering you had no such issues throughout your childhood and adult career?

I believe it was triggered when I retired early from my structured museum job to care for my mother, who has serious medical and cognitive issues. Losing my daily routine, combined with the emotional weight of caregiving and the constant travel, completely eroded my usual coping outlets like yoga and art. Over the last ten months, it all just piled up until I couldn't handle it anymore.

You've mentioned that your symptoms started after retiring to care for your mother, which is a significant life change. Can you elaborate on whether you've experienced any other significant stressors or life changes around the same time that might have contributed to your symptoms?

There weren't any other unrelated events, but the transition itself was incredibly overwhelming. Losing the structure of my museum career, the emotional toll of my mother's cognitive decline, and the grueling commutes from Rockland County to the Bronx all hit me at once. Without my usual outlets like yoga and art to ground me, the pressure just became too much to bear.

Given that your symptoms started around ten months ago, can you confirm whether you experienced any symptoms of inattention or hyperactivity during your childhood or adolescence that may have been less noticeable or not diagnosed at the time?

I don't recall having any issues with attention or hyperactivity during my childhood or adolescence. These difficulties with focus and organization only began recently, after I retired and started caring for my mother.
Can you confirm that you have had no periods of significant improvement or remission in your symptoms of inattention and hyperactivity since they began ten months ago?

Actually, these hyperactive, wired feelings have come and gone rather than being completely continuous, though they have dominated about six of the last ten months. I've had brief stretches where my energy felt closer to my old self, and even a long period in late summer where I felt flat and drained instead of revved up, even though I was still hearing voices and feeling paranoid.
Can you tell me more about the voices and paranoid feelings you mentioned, such as when they started and how often you experience them?

Those started about eight months ago and happen almost every day, especially at night when I'm sorting my mother's pillbox and clearly hear a man and a woman in the next room criticizing how I handle things. I've also become convinced that my neighbors and the museum board are coordinating through the local arts newsletter and clues on the train to judge my caregiving and push me out of the community.
Can you describe the voices you hear and the paranoid feelings in more detail, such as what the voices say and how they relate to your daily life and the perceived plot against you?

The man and woman in the next room mock me constantly, saying things like "she can't even get the pills right" while I try to organize my mother's medicine. I know they are reporting back to my neighbors and the museum board, who are using hidden clues in the local arts newsletter and on the train to judge my caregiving and coordinate a plan to push me out of the community.

Can you clarify if the voices you hear and the paranoid feelings you experience are present even when you're not feeling hyperactive or restless, or if they tend to occur together with your symptoms of inattention and hyperactivity?

They actually happen in both situations. During my highly active, sleepless periods in the spring, the voices and paranoid thoughts were very intense and occurred at the exact same time as my hyperactivity. However, there was also a long stretch in late summer when my mood felt completely flat and drained, yet I still heard the voices and felt like people were plotting against me.
Can you tell me if you have ever experienced a period where the voices and paranoid thoughts completely stopped, or have they been consistently present since they first started eight months ago?

No, they have never completely stopped since they first started eight months ago. They have been consistently there on most days, and it is just incredibly exhausting to live with this constant noise and suspicion. Even during my quietest, flattest moments, the voices and that feeling of being watched never really go away.

Have you ever experienced any periods where the voices stopped or the paranoid thoughts seemed less convincing, allowing you to question their reality, or have they consistently felt very real to you since they started?

They have consistently felt overwhelmingly real to me since they started eight months ago, and the voices of the man and woman sound completely clear, even though no one is there when I check. Even when my niece shows me emails proving that the museum board is just worried about me rather than plotting, I still can't shake the absolute conviction that they are coordinating against me.
Can you describe any periods where you questioned the reality of the voices or paranoid thoughts, or have they always felt unquestionably real to you?

They have always felt completely real to me, and the voices sound so clear that I've gone into the next room to look for the people, only to find no one there and the TV turned off. I also remain absolutely convinced that the museum board and my neighbors are coordinating against me, even when my niece shows me emails proving they are just worried about me.

Can you tell me if you have ever experienced any periods where you lost touch with reality, aside from the voices and paranoid thoughts, such as feeling like you're in a dream or detached from your body?

No, I haven't ever experienced feeling detached from my body or like I was living in a dream. My difficulties have really just been centered on the voices I hear and the sense that people are coordinating against me, but I've always felt present in my own body.
Have you ever had any episodes where the voices you hear tell you to do something, or are they primarily critical or conversational in nature?

No, they have never commanded me to do anything. Instead, they are conversational and very critical, like a man and a woman in the next room talking about me in the third person. They just comment on and criticize how I'm handling things, especially when I'm trying to sort my mother's pills.
Have you ever experienced any other types of hallucinations, such as seeing things that aren't there, or have the hallucinations been limited to hearing the voices of the man and woman?
No, I have never seen anything that wasn't there. The hallucinations have been strictly limited to hearing the voices of that man and woman talking about me from the next room.
Can you describe how the voices and paranoid thoughts have impacted your daily functioning and relationships, and have you noticed any patterns or triggers that make them worse or better?

The constant paranoia has forced me to withdraw from my docent friends and community, while those critical voices make me feel so incompetent that I neglect basic chores and miss my mother's medical appointments. They are worst at night when I am stressed and trying to manage her medications, and they flare up heavily when I'm sleep-deprived and racing, though they also lingered even during that flat, drained stretch in late summer.

Can you confirm whether the voices and paranoid thoughts have ever led you to behave in ways that are clearly in response to these hallucinations, such as changing your daily routine or avoiding certain places due to the perceived plot against you?

Yes, they have definitely changed my behavior; I completely withdrew from my beloved museum docent duties and stopped attending community events because I felt the board and my neighbors were plotting to push me out. I also find myself constantly checking the next room when I hear those voices criticizing me, and I get highly anxious and hyper-vigilant looking for "clues" whenever I ride the train.

Can you tell me if you have ever experienced a period where you had a break from both the voices and the paranoid thoughts, allowing you to function without their influence for a significant amount of time, or have they been consistently present and dominating your thoughts and behaviors?

No, I haven't had any break from them whatsoever. For the past eight months, the voices and the paranoid feelings of being plotted against have been there almost every single day, completely dominating my life. There has been no period where I felt truly free from their influence.
Have you ever experienced any periods where you felt like the voices or paranoid thoughts were not real, or have they always seemed like an absolute reality to you?

They have always felt like an absolute reality to me, because even when I go to check the next room and find nobody there, the voices still sound completely clear and real. I also remain absolutely convinced about the museum board and my neighbors plotting against me, even when my niece tries to show me reassuring emails to prove they are just worried.

Have you ever experienced a period where the voices or paranoid thoughts seemed less real or less convincing to you, allowing you to question their validity, or have they consistently felt like an absolute reality since they started?

They have consistently felt like an absolute, undeniable reality to me, and I have never been able to question their validity. Even though I find no one in the next room when I check and my niece shows me emails proving there is no plot, I still feel absolutely convinced in the moment. I simply cannot shake the feeling that it is all completely real.
Can you describe if the voices you hear and the paranoid thoughts you experience are present at the same time as your symptoms of disorganization and hyperactivity, or do they occur separately?

They actually occur both together and separately. During a highly energetic, sleepless phase in the spring when I was racing around trying to plan an art festival, the voices and paranoid beliefs were happening at the exact same time. But in late summer, my high energy completely subsided and my mood felt flat, yet the voices and thoughts about the board plotting against me continued on their own for weeks.

Can you confirm whether the voices you hear and the paranoid thoughts you experience have ever led you to behave in ways that put you or others at risk of harm, due to acting on the hallucinations or delusions?

No, I have never acted on the voices or my beliefs about the museum board in a way that caused harm. While I have done some risky things like speeding on the highway or meeting up with a stranger online, those actions only happened when I was in a highly driven, wired phase rather than as a direct reaction to the voices.

Can you tell me if you have ever experienced any periods where the voices or paranoid thoughts seemed to influence your hyperactive or disorganized behavior, or have they always felt separate from those symptoms?

They have always felt quite separate in terms of what actually drives them. My pacing, cleaning, and frantic project planning feel like they are fueled by a strange, hyperactive energy inside me, rather than being a reaction to the voices or the plot. Even when they were happening at the exact same time in the spring, the wired behavior and the voices felt like two distinct things occurring at once.
Can you describe any instances where your hyperactive or disorganized behavior seemed to be directly triggered by the voices or paranoid thoughts, rather than just occurring at the same time?
I'm not really sure if one directly triggered the other. They mostly just seemed to happen at the same time and felt like a chaotic mix of everything going on at once.
Have you ever experienced any other types of psychotic symptoms, such as disorganized thinking or behavior, aside from the voices and paranoid thoughts?

Yes, my thinking gets very disorganized; my mind will ricochet from my mother's neurologist to paintings I saw in college, making me ramble in circles and never finish a thought. I also struggle with disorganized behaviors, like pacing endlessly while rearranging medical forms and art catalogs, muttering to myself, and suddenly freezing in place in the hallway for long stretches.
